# Styling & Tailwind setup

app-shell ships its own compiled styles and a set of themes. In **your** app you write **ordinary Tailwind classes** — the `astw:` prefix you may see in app-shell's own source is an **internal** prefix for the library's shipped stylesheet and is not something consumers use.

## 1. Install Tailwind

```bash
pnpm add -D tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite
```

## 2. Add the Vite plugin

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite";
import { defineConfig } from "vite";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()],
});
```

## 3. Import Tailwind + the app-shell theme

Import Tailwind first, then app-shell's base styles, then one theme:

```css
/* src/index.css */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@tailor-platform/app-shell/styles";
@import "@tailor-platform/app-shell/themes/bloom";
```

## 4. Use ordinary Tailwind in your code

Your own markup uses unprefixed utilities; app-shell components bring their own styling:

```tsx
import { Button } from "@tailor-platform/app-shell";

<div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
  <Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>
  <Button>Save</Button>
</div>;
```

> **Do not** use the `astw:` prefix in your app — it is reserved for app-shell's internal stylesheet. If you see it in generated example code, that's a bug in the example (report it).

## Reference implementation

The docs explorer app (`examples/docs-app`) and the Vite example (`examples/vite-app`) are both wired exactly this way — use them as a copy-paste reference.
